European Surveillance

Parliament Rebuffs Chat Control as Devs Build for the Mesh

European Parliament blocks Council deal on Chat Control mass scanning as protocol developers push mesh and offline communications beyond state borders.

By the Dispatches Desk

The European Parliament has once again derailed the European Council's flagship mass scanning deal, known across the continent as Chat Control 2.0. Lyudmyla Kozlovska, reporting the vote from Brussels, noted that lawmakers firmly rejected blanket surveillance mandates, automated search plans, and administrative scanning orders issued without judicial warrants. Yet her warning to decentralized networks remained stark: Any #relay or client operating in the #EU could face obligations under this framework.

Rather than waiting on legislative margins, protocol engineers across Nostr are treating policy threats as network routing failures. Cody revealed PsstPsst, a dedicated communications application designed to operate entirely without internet connectivity: Chat even when you’re offline. Built upon NIP-17 direct messaging and NIP-4e key separation, PsstPsst routes encrypted messages locally across Bluetooth and plans future integration with FIPS mesh standards. Simultaneously, researchers demonstrated Cashu ecash tokens moving offline across Apple's Find My Bluetooth Low Energy mesh via the find-my-nuts proof-of-concept.

Dispatches cited: Lyudmyla Kozlovska · Cody on PsstPsst.

Autumn Reflections

What the Winter Was For

As price mania recedes, the timeline sharpens its focus on custody, capture, and the discipline of quiet seasons.

By the Essay Desk

A year after retail euphoria and ticker-watching dominated every channel, an unmistakable stillness has settled across the network. Contra, reflecting in an extensive essay on the cycle's hangover, caught the prevailing sentiment: Scroll your feed this fall and count the laser eyes still up. You won't need both hands. What remains in place of hype is sober engineering and ideological clarity: Now the talk runs lower, and on Nostr it has curdled into something sharper.

That introspection echoed in reading lists across the feed. Gigi marked an essay asking foundational questions about the architecture of modern networks: What if we built the Internet badly? Meanwhile, DanConwayDev reminded systems developers of Linux's ancient first commandment: WE DO NOT BREAK USERSPACE!

Systems, Custody & Software

Security & Exchange

Bisq Releases v1.10.9; Mostro Demystifies Escrow

Critical security audits prompt mandatory trader upgrades as Lightning hold invoices prove their utility.

Bisq issued release v1.10.9, incorporating critical fixes discovered in its recent security audit alongside updated Tor binaries. The developers issued a direct mandate to users: Updating to this version is required to continue trading.

At the same time, decentralized exchange Mostro explained the mechanics powering its non-custodial Lightning escrow: A hold invoice is the reason Mostro 🧌 can run escrow without ever touching your sats. Sellers lock funds directly within their own wallets until trade completion, avoiding custodial liability.

Sources: Bisq announcement · Mostro explanation.

Software Craft

Between Ninja Devs and Vibe Coders

A debate breaks out over code quality, generational tooling, and agentic mobile development.

A fiery exchange over developer standards gripped technical channels. Developer Nour laid out the critique plainly: I feel just a little feeling that literally nobody has a fucking clue about software engineering. As modern AI tools prompt a wave of automated prototypes, Nour observed that the ancient warrior ninja devs are coming out of their multiplexer caves to teach how real code bases look like.

Yet the democratization of tools is undeniable. Highlights marked by thepurpose from Max showed how accessible development has become: a beginner can now build and share a modest Android app under a chosen identity, directing an open-source coding agent from a phone. Breno Brito highlighted the broader transformation: "The craft of writing code will disappear. Yes, there are still Italian shoe makers around. But look at your feet."

Dispatches: Nour's reflection · thepurpose highlight · Breno Brito highlight.

Software Catalog

Fresh Binaries on Zapstore and Gitworkshop

New utilities arrive on decentralized app indices alongside fresh open source repositories.

Zapstore’s catalog recorded significant new application entries today:

• BTC Map — The global index of merchants accepting Bitcoin on-chain and over Lightning.

• MBCompass — Open-source navigation, GPX export, and offline map tracking that refuses telemetry.

• Quiet Dial — Granular volume controls that drop below Android's default hardware minimums.

• DeadHash — Hash generation utility supporting MD5, SHA-256, SHA-512, and CRC32.

Over on gitworkshop.dev, Snick published the repository for SeedHammer viewer, while arbadacarba updated gittr.
